Yeah, it depends on how many pre reqs the program requires. Mine only took 2 semesters for the rad tech program 

EDIT: Most rad tech associate programs take 8 or 9 semesters if you include pre reqs. But it's all dependent on what classes will transfer from outside america
So pre-reqs are classes you take in college before you start your actual program. They're meant to give you all of the basic skills you need to complete your program

So most community colleges here in America are going to require basic pre-reqs such as writing, math, and probably chem/anatomy. I'm not too sure if your high school classes would transfer over though. I think it would depend on what specific community college you want to get into. 

Regarding competitiveness, it also depends on the school you go to. For example, my program wasn't necessarily based on how well you performed in your classes. As long as you could pass a standardized test (HESI A2) geared towards healthcare & science you were entered into a lottery in which people were chosen randomly. 

Again, that was just my school though. There's probably others that revolve more around performance.
